title: Control language mapping: SOC2 / ISO / HIPAA evidence and seller scripts
body:
Purpose: A concise reference for sellers and solutions engineers that maps common customer compliance questions to Redwood-ready control language, the precise evidence artifacts we can deliver, and short/long replies for calls and RFP responses. This is not legal text; it is a go-to-market translation layer to speed diligence and reduce back-and-forth with security reviewers.

Scope: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 alignment notes, HIPAA (BAA) readiness items, and canonical descriptions of data handling, key management, and audit telemetry. Covers Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment flavors where behavior diverges.

How to use this doc:
- Quick claim lines: one- or two-sentence statements sellers can use in early conversations.
- Evidence map: for each claim, the list of artifacts we can provide (reports, config screenshots, sample logs, retention policies).
- Script snippets: short (30s) and expanded (2–3 min) answers for calls.
- Escalation triggers: when to route to Security/Legal/Engineering for deeper evidence.

1) Data residency & access claim
- Quick claim: "Customers can choose regional hosting and can restrict inference traffic to their VPC for Private or Dedicated deployments; hosted customers can select region-level options at provisioning."
- Evidence artifacts: data residency map (regions list), Dedicated/VPC deployment diagram, network isolation checklist, SOC2 coverage scope doc (shows control scoping).
- Short script: "For regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private—both support region pinning and network isolation; we can share a VPC diagram and a sample network ACL during diligence."
- Expanded reply: describe exact network boundaries, where plaintext request bodies exist (ingress nodes for hosted API vs. customer-managed gateways for Private), and mention encryption-in-transit and at-rest with KMS integration.
- Escalation: customer asks for formal data flow diagram marked with names of subnets or provider account IDs -> route to solutions engineering with architecture review.

2) Audit logs & telemetry claim
- Quick claim: "We capture tamper-evident audit telemetry across control plane events, model deployments, and admin actions; logs can be exported to customer SIEM in standard formats."
- Evidence artifacts: sample audit-log extract (redacted), log schema doc, export runbook to S3/Cloud Logging, sample retention policy, SOC2 audit evidence indexing.
- Short script: "We produce structured audit events for administrative actions and model rollouts, and can forward those to your SIEM. Heres a redacted example and a schema PDF we share with auditors."
- Expanded reply: list log fields (timestamp, actor id, action, resource, source IP, request id, before/after for config changes), explain HMAC/timestamp sequencing for tamper evidence, and note retention controls per offering (hosted default 90 days, Dedicated: configurable via contract, Private: customer-controlled).
- Recommended RFP language (snippet): "Redwood will provide exported audit logs for control-plane events in JSON or Syslog format, with a schema that includes actor, action, resource, timestamp, and request identifier. Retention period for hosted deployments is 90 days by default; contractual retention can be extended for Dedicated customers."

3) PII handling & minimization claim
- Quick claim: "We do not train models on customer data; customers retain control of their data and can opt into KV/prefix caching and redaction settings to limit persistent storage."
- Evidence artifacts: data handling playbook excerpt, training policy statement, sample cache-control settings screenshot, SOC2 CC6 evidence where applicable.
- Short script: "Customer inputs are used to produce real-time inference and — except where caching is explicitly enabled — are not used to update models. We can share the specific flag names, default values, and a redacted cache snapshot to auditors."
- Expanded reply: clarify differences across offerings: Hosted has automated prefix caching optimizations with opt-out; Dedicated and Private allow explicit configs and on-prem control. Share sample config file lines and a recorded demo showing cache clear operation.

4) Key management and encryption claim
- Quick claim: "Data is encrypted in-transit and at-rest; customers can integrate their KMS for Dedicated and Private deployments to manage at-rest keys."
- Evidence artifacts: TLS cert lifecycle policy, KMS integration guide, sample CMEK (customer-managed encryption key) manifest, SOC2 control narrative for encryption.
- Short script: "We use TLS 1.2+ for all external traffic. For Dedicated and Private deployments you can bring your own keys (KMS/HSM) and control rotation cadence."
- Expanded reply: provide the technical flow (encryption atop persistence layer, per-tenant key wrapping, KMS API calls with least-privileged service account), and include a screenshot of the KMS IAM policy template we provide.

5) Incident response & breach notification claim
- Quick claim: "Redwood has a documented IR process tied into our incident management platform and provides contractual breach notification SLAs for enterprise agreements."
- Evidence artifacts: summary incident response playbook, past SOC2 penetration testing cadence, notification SLA clause examples, post-incident root-cause report template.
- Short script: "We maintain an incident runbook and will notify impacted customers within the contracted SLA window; for Dedicated customers we offer a higher-notice tier and can coordinate joint response playbooks."

6) Model fallback and graceful degradation claim
- Quick claim: "We support automated fallback to compatible model variants and region routing to preserve availability while meeting data residency constraints."
- Evidence artifacts: routing policy matrix, fallback logs snippet, canary rollout checklist, latency SLO chart.
- Short script: "If capacity is constrained we can fall back to a pre-approved variant automatically; we surface that event in the audit logs and in the console per-request tracing."

Sales rebuttals to common pushbacks (one-liners):
- "We can’t provide raw logs for privacy reasons" -> "We provide redacted, schema-annotated audit extracts and a verifiable export path; for Dedicated/Private you can host the log sink directly."
- "How do I prove logs weren’t tampered after export?" -> "We can show log sequencing and HMAC/timestamping evidence and provide a verifier script to reproduce integrity checks."
- "We need a longer retention window" -> "Retention is negotiable for Dedicated contracts and fully customer-controlled for Private; hosted defaults are a starting point we can extend contractually."

Packaging the evidence bundle (recommended contents):
- Cover memo with scope and date range (one page).
- Signed SOC2 or ISO summary (if available) and index of covered systems.
- Redacted sample logs and schema.
- Key management appendix with KMS integration guide.
- Network/VPC diagrams per deployment type.
- Sample contractual clause snippets (notification SLA, retention, data residency).
- Contact sheet for Security/SE/Legal with escalation phone/email.

Suggested seller flow for a first procurement contact:
1) Intro call: open with Quick claims (30s) and ask whether customer requires BAA/SOC2/ISO evidence.
2) If yes, offer an "evidence bundle" delivery within 3 business days (redacted) and schedule an architecture deep-dive.
3) If they request specific artifacts, map ask to Evidence Map and own it in the support ticket with SE and Security cced.

Escalation matrix (when to involve which team):
- Legal: contract language negotiations or exceptions to standard retention/KMS terms.
- Security: requests for raw logs, cryptographic proofs, or detailed control test evidence.
- Engineering/SE: architecture walk-throughs, region placement diagrams, and vendor-specific integrations.

Open questions / decisions to finalize:
- Hosted retention default: confirm whether 90 days is still the company default for hosted audit logs or whether we should move to 30/60/90 tiers in the public docs.
- Standard export formats: choose primary canonical format (JSON vs. CEF vs. Syslog) for the evidence bundle.
- Template for redaction: define standardized automatic redaction rules for sample logs we provide to prospects.

Appendix: short legal snippets for RD to propose to Legal (for SE use only, not final legal text):
- "Export of Logs: Provider will export control-plane audit logs for the contracted tenant in JSON or Syslog format on request, redacted for PII where required, within 5 business days. Retention and delivery method to be mutually agreed in the SOW for Dedicated contracts."
- "KMS: For Dedicated and Private deployments, Customer may provide KMS credentials and manage keys. Provider will implement key wrapping and will not retain plaintext keys in its control plane."

Next steps and owners:
- Finalize hosted retention default and publish in the public FAQ (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-12).
- Create standardized redacted log sample set for sales (owner: Diego Martinez, due: 2026-03-19).
- Legal to review suggested contract snippets and return markups (owner: Lena Hoffmann, due: 2026-03-22).

Notes to reviewers: please flag anything that sounds like definitive legal commitment. The goal is to have tidy, seller-friendly claims that are traceable to concrete artifacts we can actually deliver in 3 business days for first-level diligence.
